rows.corroboration: The committed corpus index records pageCount: null and acroFieldCount: null for all five, and for no other form in this lane's reach. Whatever built that index could not open them either.
rows.whatWasNotClaimed: This lane did not test another PDF reader against these files, because it has none, and so states nothing about whether some other reader could open them. The finding is about this toolchain, and it is stated as such.
rows.countersNote: No counters are returned. A counter set implies a censused form, and no form here was censused. Returning nine zeros for a family that rendered nothing would be the worst possible row.
findingsRaisedForOthers: BLOCKING for this family, owner of the acquisition pipeline: all five California Judicial Council forms in the Master Library are encrypted PDFs — CR-106, MC-025 and MC-031 with /V 4 /R 4, CR-180 and CR-181 with /V 5 /R 6 AES-256. They bind by exact SHA-256 and cannot be read. This family cannot be built until either the corpus carries decrypted-at-acquisition copies of these five, with their own recorded custody, or the toolchain gains a reader that decrypts. Both are decisions above this lane.

The same condition holds for WV SCA-C903, returned separately in the PF10 row. The two are one problem, not two: whatever acquired these files preserved the publisher's encryption, and every downstream family that needs one of them stops in the same place.
